question: Should the supported filesystem policy be a file-tool-only boundary with an explicit exec exclusion, or must the first supported security contract also restrict shell-mediated filesystem access?
rationale: This choice determines the user-facing security guarantee, config shape, compatibility migration, and which of the open candidate implementations can land safely; it cannot be inferred from source alone.

options.title: Define a scoped file-tool policy
options.body: Adopt normalized deny-wins rules for file-capable tools, preserve compatibility deliberately, and document that arbitrary exec is outside the v1 security boundary.

options.title: Require an exec-capable boundary
options.body: Do not merge a filesystem-sandbox claim until the design also constrains shell-mediated reads, writes, redirects, and command working directories.

options.title: Keep current workspace-only mode
options.body: Retain the existing boolean confinement while deferring granular policy work until the execution-boundary design is approved.

recommendation.title: Define a scoped file-tool policy
recommendation.body: Adopt normalized deny-wins rules for file-capable tools, preserve compatibility deliberately, and document that arbitrary exec is outside the v1 security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied discussion and prior review connect steipete directly to the unresolved policy and execution-boundary decision.
